messages:
sara (support): Customer reports users getting 403 on SSO immediately after IdP cert rotation. Some users succeed, others fail. attaching snippet of SP log: 

sara (support): log: "SAML response rejected: Recipient mismatch. expected=https://sp.acme-app.com/saml/acs got=https://sp.acme-app.com:8443/saml/acs"

mike (customer): Confirmed. Our IdP rotated signing certs via automation at 2026-02-23T14:31:50Z and pushed metadata to your metadata endpoint. Most users see login success but a subset behind a legacy proxy fail.

devon (sre): Any chance a proxy or CDN is rewriting Host/Port? That port in the Recipient looks like an origin port rather than public URL. :eyes:

sara (support): Customer says they front with a legacy proxy that rewrites origin headers and health probes use port 8443. I captured a raw SAML assertion snippet from a failing user: 

```xml
<saml:Assertion ...>
  <saml:Subject>
    <saml:SubjectConfirmation Method="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:cm:bearer">
      <saml:SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://sp.acme-app.com:8443/saml/acs" NotOnOrAfter="..."/>
    </saml:SubjectConfirmation>
  </saml:Subject>
</saml:Assertion>
```

ingrid (platform): That exact pattern matched a previous incident where the edge proxy added the origin port into the assertion recipient. Our SP does strict recipient comparison by default. Two immediate options: accept recipient both with and without port as a temporary fallback, or canonicalize incoming Host header before validation.

kevin (eng): Quick triage note: SP metadata lists ACS as https://sp.acme-app.com/saml/acs (no port). When IdP signs an assertion where Recipient contains :8443, signature is still valid, but our recipient check fails. We should avoid relaxing checks long-term. Short-term fallback is acceptable with logging.

devon (sre): Steps I recommend to test/fix quickly:
1) Force metadata refresh on SP (we saw stale IdP keys in one instance).
2) Check metadata fetch logs for 302/redirect handling (customer said their metadata endpoint does a redirect).
3) Add a temporary tolerant recipient check on a small canary fleet (accept with/without :8443) and enable extra debug logging for recipient mismatches.

sara (support): I ran a manual metadata refresh on the affected SP instance: `POST /admin/metadata/refresh?force` and restarted the auth worker. Result: about half the failing users still 403.

saml-bot: automated note: IdP metadata last-fetched=2026-02-23T14:32:09Z, cert-thumbprint=AB:CD:EF:12:34, cert-rotated=2026-02-23T14:31:50Z, fetch-followed-redirect=true

mike (customer): We verified our automation posts a new metadata file and the endpoint returns a 302 -> /metadata/latest which contains the new cert. We rely on your metadata polling. Our side shows no errors.

ingrid (platform): Two likely contributors: (A) short one-minute rotation/fetch skew where some SPs hit metadata right before refresh and kept the old key until TTL expired, (B) proxy injecting :8443 into assertions. We'll pursue both: force metadata refresh across all SPs + patch to canonicalize recipient comparison.

kevin (eng): Action items for eng:
- Add a metadata-change detector: if cert-thumbprint in fetched metadata != cached thumbprint then immediate reload (bypass TTL).
- Add optional recipient canonicalization config (strip origin port) behind a canary flag.
- Improve logging to include raw Recipient and expected ACS URL to speed triage.

devon (sre): Quick mitigation deployed to canary: accept recipient both with and without :8443. Canary login success rate improved from ~40% to ~98%. We'll keep the toggle for 2 hours and monitor.

sara (support): Customer updated: login success improved after canary. They still want root cause fix on metadata polling and a note to fix proxy behavior. I've scheduled a joint call with their infra team to stop exposing origin port in SAML.

mike (customer): Thanks, can you also document repro steps so our SREs can validate when we next rotate?

kevin (eng): Repro steps for customer's SREs:
1) Rotate IdP signing cert and publish new metadata via your endpoint which responds with an HTTP 302 to /metadata/latest.
2) From a client behind an origin-proxy that rewrites Host to include :8443, perform SSO flow to produce assertion with Recipient containing :8443.
3) On SP, observe recipient mismatch rejection in auth logs.
4) Force metadata refresh on SP, verify if cached key updates.

ingrid (platform): I'll open a follow-up task for persistent fixes: immediate TTL-bypass on thumbprint change + optional recipient canonicalization + docs for customers about avoiding origin-port in SAML recipients.

sara (support): Thanks team — closing high-priority escalations loop for now. Will reopen if customer sees regressions. :thumbsup:
